statement: container.rs implements the crypto-v1 encrypted INDEXED container: two sections (CryptoEnvelope kind 32, EncryptedSegments kind 33, section magic EBS1), a 192-byte footer v2, 64-byte SegmentHeaders and 32-byte ProtectedRecordHeaders, CONTROL=1/PAYLOAD=2 segment classes and DATA=1/END=2 record classes.
evidence_in_source: constants in code; normative source docs/crypto-wire-v1.md

statement: Frozen segment capacities: at most 2^20-1 DATA records per segment, 1 GiB unpadded private DATA per segment, 1 MiB private-record capacity for CONTROL and 64 MiB for PAYLOAD.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md §Segments, padding, and chunk boundaries L137-146
research_needed: Measure throughput, memory and random-access cost as functions of record/segment capacity to justify 1 MiB/64 MiB/1 GiB/2^20-1 choices.
decision_needed: Are the CONTROL/PAYLOAD record capacities and segment limits final for v1?

statement: EncryptedWriteOptions carries recipients, optional password, padding mode, boundary mode, include_index flag, and embedded signatures; Default is no recipients, no password, Bucketed padding, SecretGearTable boundary, Index included, no signatures.
Default chunk-boundary mode is SECRET_GEAR_TABLE; the suite document treats analogous secret-table keyed CDC as broken in research and only defense in depth, while stronger PHTE_AES128 is opt-in.
evidence_in_source: inference from code default plus primary-citation discussion in suite doc (Truong et al. CCS 2025)
research_needed: Security analysis of boundary leakage of secret Gear table under bucketed padding; measure PHTE throughput/dedup cost vs Gear to see if PHTE can be default.
decision_needed: Should PHTE_AES128 become the default encrypted boundary mode for v1?

statement: EncryptedOpenOptions::new pairs optional unlock material with CryptoPolicy::default and the bootstrap resource and decode policies; callers can override crypto, resource, and decode policies independently.
PublicCryptoInspection (keyless) exposes: encrypted flag, payload suite name, recipient count, per-stanza recipient types, padding mode, boundary mode, segment count, and total container bytes.
research_needed: Privacy evaluation of what recipient count, segment count and total size reveal about archive contents.

statement: public_inspection labels stanza type 1 as xwing-draft-10, type 2 as password-argon2id, anything else as unknown, and reports fixed payload suite string entrybound-payload-suite-v1; segment count includes the terminal segment.

AuthenticatedDescriptorInspection reports encrypted Descriptor record version, whether a producer resource declaration is present, an independently_validated flag, and the declared budget/decode requirements when present.

inspect_encrypted hard-codes independently_validated=true and infers record_version 2 solely from the private-resource-declaration feature bit; truth of the flag rests on open_encrypted having succeeded rather than a separate check.
research_needed: Confirm that every successful open_encrypted path enforces declared-vs-actual resource and decode equality so the constant claim is sound.

statement: AuthenticatedEncryptedArchive returns the verified OpenedArchive, embedded signatures, private recipient directory entries (stanza ID, type, fingerprint, label) and an AddressingBinding; the archive file key is never exposed.

encrypt_archive encrypts an already-planned EAM: it rewrites planner_id by prefix to fast/balanced/dense/extreme-enc-v1, prepares encrypted plain parts, draws a fresh random 32-byte AFK and archive ID from the OS CSPRNG, then seals.

encrypt_archive never re-chunks with the AFK-derived boundary key: chunk boundaries come from the caller's plan (typically public-Gear plan_directory), yet the envelope records the boundary mode and planner_id is relabelled -enc-v1, so keyed-CDC protection silently does not apply to library callers.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md L152-156 (encrypted creation derives secret Gear/PHTE boundaries)
evidence_in_source: inference from code; all crypto_v1.rs and random_access.rs tests call plan_directory then encrypt_archive; only pack_directory_encrypted (mod.rs) keys chunking
research_needed: Confirm chunker_id of encrypt_archive output; assess boundary leakage for archives produced this way.
decision_needed: Should encrypt_archive refuse unkeyed plans, replan with keyed CDC, or be made crate-private?

statement: encrypted_planner_id leaves planner IDs without a fast-/balanced-/dense-/extreme- prefix unchanged, so an encrypted archive may carry a non -enc-v1 planner ID.
decision_needed: Should encryption refuse EAMs whose planner ID does not map to a frozen profile?

statement: encrypt_with_file_key (pub(super)) accepts caller-supplied AFK and archive ID; it is the seam used by pack_directory_encrypted, rotation, and in-crate tests with fixed key material; no public deterministic-encryption API exists.

Writer feature bits: ordinary incompat bits plus ENCRYPTED_INDEXED_V1, PAYLOAD_SUITE_V1, PADDING, and exactly one of XWING/PASSWORD recipient; STRONG_BOUNDARY iff PhteAes128; SIGNATURE_ED25519_V1 iff embedded signatures. PADDING is set even for PaddingMode::None.

Writer emits encrypted Descriptor v1 or v2 according to the plain parts; v2 additionally sets FEATURE_PRIVATE_RESOURCE_DECLARATION_V1 (0x1000); any other Descriptor version is refused as private-object invalid.

Corrected writer emits Descriptor v2 with the private-resource feature, while legacy pre-correction Descriptor-v1 encrypted archives remain readable with budget_declared false; v2 declarations are enforced against caller resource and decode policy (ResourceLimit).
decision_needed: How long must readers keep accepting pre-correction Descriptor-v1 encrypted archives?

statement: CryptoEnvelope contains archive ID, HMAC key commitment (binding versions, suite, archive ID, layout, padding, boundary), protection policy, padding mode, boundary mode, canonical stanzas and an envelope MAC over public context, commitment, policy and stanza sequence.
Recipient stanzas are sorted by their canonical sort key before MAC and encoding; the writer panics via expect if a stanza lacks a canonical sort key.
evidence_in_source: code; reorder/duplicate tampering test crypto_v1.rs L446-477

statement: Private object emission order: Descriptor, TransformPlans, ChunkGroups (cross-file), RecipientDirectory (hybrid), Dictionaries (cross-file), ReconstructionData (reconstructive), ReconstructionRegions (whole-object), Chunk frames, Manifest, Fidelity, Signatures (optional), Index (optional), then terminal ArchiveFinal.

Writer places exactly one private object in each segment, so public segment count equals control-object count plus unique Chunk count plus terminal, and each PAYLOAD segment extent reveals its Chunk's padded size bucket.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-threat-model-v1.md L183-192 (record count and bucket leakage acknowledged)
evidence_in_source: inference from code: build_unique_segment called with a single object per ordinal
research_needed: Quantify content-inference risk from exact unique-Chunk count and per-Chunk bucket sequence on realistic corpora; evaluate multi-object segments as mitigation.
decision_needed: Should the writer pack multiple objects per segment to hide unique Chunk count?

statement: Encrypted Index entries (record 27) carry Chunk digest, segment ordinal, first protected-record counter always 0, and fragment count; entries are sorted and emitted only when include_index is true.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-wire-v1.md §Private recipient directory and encrypted Index entries L554-568

statement: Embedded signatures are validated by encoding, sorted by encoded bytes, and an exact duplicate aborts creation with CryptoPrivateObjectInvalid.

When re-encrypting for mutation, prior PAYLOAD segments are reused byte-for-byte at the same ordinal if class matches; their salts are pre-registered and any duplicate reused salt or class mismatch is refused.
Segment salts must be unique per (class, salt) within one archive: the writer retries up to 16 fresh OS-random salts, then refuses with CryptoResourcePolicyRefused; readers reject any reuse.
evidence_in_source: code at container.rs:2018-2037 and reader check container.rs:1319-1321

statement: ArchiveFinalV1 (record 25) has 12 tags: total segment count, entry count, total logical bytes, unique Chunk count, LAI, PCR, AUX, recipient-set digest, prior segment-sequence digest, FooterCore digest, Descriptor object ID, Manifest object ID.

The writer predicts the terminal segment extent using a dummy ArchiveFinal, computes footer locators and FooterCore before sealing the real terminal segment, and refuses if the terminal extent changes.

Physical layout: 256-byte preamble, CryptoEnvelope section at offset 256, EncryptedSegments section immediately after, 192-byte footer at EOF; ArchiveFinal sits 64 bytes into the terminal segment; PCI is SHA-256 identity over the complete encrypted bytes.

Encrypted creation requires exactly one protection method: X-Wing recipients or one password, never both nor neither (PolicyRefused CryptoRecipientPolicyInvalid); more than 1024 recipients is refused; duplicate recipient fingerprints are refused; embedded signatures must encode.
Mixed protection (hybrid public-key recipients plus a password) and multiple passwords are refused; PASSWORD_ONLY archives hold exactly one password stanza.
decision_needed: Is mixed password-plus-recipient protection a post-v1 requirement?

statement: Library creation accepts an empty password (Some of empty bytes) because validate_write_options checks only presence; change_password and the CLI change-password path reject empty new passwords, and CLI pack only checks confirmation equality.
evidence_in_source: code container.rs:526 vs container.rs:873-881 and entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:709-716, 2825-2828
research_needed: Usability and security review of minimum password policy for Argon2id-protected archives.
decision_needed: Should encrypted creation reject empty or weak passwords at the library boundary?

statement: Password stanzas use fixed Argon2id v1.3 creation parameters m=262144 KiB (256 MiB), t=3, p=4 with a random 16-byte salt; stanza type 2, protection class 2, random stanza ID and wrap nonce, zero recipient hint.
evidence_in_source: constants; RFC 9106 KAT in tests/crypto_primitives.rs argon2id_rfc_9106_vector
research_needed: Benchmark unlock latency and memory feasibility on low-memory/mobile/CI devices and remote-range scenarios; compare with RFC 9106 recommended profiles.

statement: Callers cannot choose Argon2id cost at creation; parameters are hard-coded although readers accept m 65536..1048576 KiB, t 3..10, p 1..16 under CryptoPolicy.
decision_needed: Should creators be able to raise or lower Argon2id cost within the frozen bounds?

statement: X-Wing recipient stanzas: type 1, class 1, method parameters naming xwing-mlkem768-x25519-sha3-256/draft-10, 1120-byte encapsulation, random stanza ID and wrap nonce; the AFK is wrapped with AES-256-GCM-SIV under an HKDF key from the shared secret.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-wire-v1.md §RecipientStanzaV1 L262-298 and §Recipient wrapping wire rules L719-744
evidence_in_source: V5 wrapping vectors in mod.rs tests; X-Wing draft-10 KATs in tests/crypto_primitives.rs every_authoritative_xwing_draft10_kat

statement: The recipient KEM is frozen to X-Wing draft-10 (ML-KEM-768 + X25519 + SHA3-256) identified by method string and inspect label; no algorithm negotiation exists.
research_needed: Track IETF X-Wing/hybrid KEM finalization for incompatible changes versus draft-10; plan migration of a draft-identified stanza type.
decision_needed: How will archives migrate if the final X-Wing specification differs from draft-10?

statement: Recipient hints are always 16 zero bytes and no public-key fingerprint is serialized publicly; unlocking therefore requires trial processing of stanzas.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-threat-model-v1.md L175-176 (hints fixed to zero in v1)

statement: Recipient directory entries are sorted by bytes 28..44 of each encoded record, i.e. the stanza ID position under the current canonical record layout.
research_needed: Conformance vector confirming directory order equals stanza-ID ascending as the spec requires.

statement: open_encrypted_authenticated: parse and bound public framing, require unlock (else CryptoNoMatchingRecipient), unlock envelope, decrypt and verify all segments, drop AFK, build AddressingBinding (suite, recipient-set digest, commitment, archive ID), then open plain parts under resource/decode policy with PCI.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md L167-171 (materialize only after full verification)

statement: verify_encrypted requires full unlock and returns the ordinary VerificationReport; authenticated verification is impossible without credentials, while keyless inspect_encrypted checks only public digests and structure.
decision_needed: Is keyless structural verification (public digests only) sufficient for custodians without keys?

statement: Encrypted write and open operate on whole in-memory byte buffers and complete EAMs (Vec output, &[u8] input); no streaming or bounded-memory encrypted writer or full reader exists.
research_needed: Measure peak memory for encrypting/opening archives larger than RAM; design bounded staging for encrypted INDEXED output.
decision_needed: Must v1 support encrypted archives larger than available memory?

statement: decrypt_segments always clones every PAYLOAD segment into a reuse map, even for ordinary open/verify where it is discarded, roughly doubling ciphertext-proportional memory.
research_needed: Profile peak memory of open_encrypted versus archive size.

statement: embed_signature fully unlocks, rejects an exact duplicate signature, re-authenticates CONTROL segments and footer while retaining AFK, archive ID, padding, boundary mode, Index presence and PAYLOAD ciphertext, then self-verifies the replacement.

add_recipient (HYBRID_ONLY only) rejects an already-present fingerprint, wraps the existing AFK for the new X-Wing recipient, preserves archive ID, keyed chunking, signatures and PAYLOAD ciphertext, rebuilds the directory, and self-verifies.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L840-842 (CRYPTO-030); docs/crypto-review-v1.md L456 (AR-18: add preserves AFK, addressing stale, PCR unchanged)

statement: Recipient addition is refused for PASSWORD_ONLY archives; there is no way to add a public-key recipient or second password to a password archive without re-creating it.
decision_needed: Should converting PASSWORD_ONLY to HYBRID_ONLY (or adding credentials) be supported?

statement: Any party able to unlock (any current recipient) may add recipients or, via reencrypt_recipients, remove all others including the creator; no owner or administrator role constrains key management.
evidence_in_source: inference from code: only unlock is required
research_needed: Threat-model review of recipient-controlled key management in shared-archive workflows.
decision_needed: Is recipient-equals-administrator acceptable for v1 key management semantics?

statement: Mutations carry prior embedded signatures forward unchanged; after add_recipient the signature's content and physical bindings stay Valid but its addressing binding becomes Stale.
decision_needed: Should mutations drop, flag, or require re-signing of signatures whose addressing binding becomes stale?

statement: Recipient removal is only by fresh encryption epoch: archive must be HYBRID_ONLY, retained list nonempty, unique, and a proper subset of the authenticated directory; otherwise PolicyRefused CryptoRecipientPolicyInvalid.
evidence_in_source: test crypto_v1.rs L260-274 (removed identity gets CryptoNoMatchingRecipient)

statement: A full re-key that keeps every current recipient (proactive AFK rotation without removal) is refused because retained must be a strict subset; simultaneous add-and-remove is also not offered.
decision_needed: Should v1 offer rotation of AFK/archive ID without removing any recipient?

statement: On removal the new recipient directory is built from caller-supplied retained XWingRecipient values, so labels come from the caller (read_file yields empty labels) rather than the authenticated directory; existing labels may be lost.
decision_needed: Should rotation preserve authenticated directory labels for retained recipients?

statement: change_password requires a PASSWORD_ONLY archive and nonempty new password and performs full re-encryption with a fresh AFK and archive ID; the old password then fails with CryptoNoMatchingRecipient.

rotate_encryption_epoch draws fresh AFK and archive ID, derives a new boundary key for the same boundary mode, replans the archive with keyed CDC for the profile inferred from planner_id, reuses padding/Index flag/signatures, and self-verifies. Tests show LAI and AUX preserved and PCI changed.

Rotation re-chunks under a new secret boundary key, so PCR (and physical signature bindings) likely change, and addressing bindings (archive ID, commitment) necessarily change, yet old embedded signatures are carried into the new epoch.
evidence_in_source: inference; tests assert only LAI/AUX equality after rotation
research_needed: Verify PCR and signature binding statuses after reencrypt_recipients/change_password.
decision_needed: Should rotated archives retain signatures that can no longer be fully valid?

statement: Removal and password change require full decryption, replanning (re-chunking and recompression) and re-encryption of the entire archive in memory; cost scales with archive size.
research_needed: Benchmark time and peak memory of reencrypt_recipients and change_password on multi-GB archives.

statement: verify_mutation_output re-derives keys from the new AFK and checks commitment, envelope MAC, every segment and the plain EAM before returning, so mutators verify replacements without holding retained recipients' private identities.

Rotation maps planner_id to a creation profile only by fast-/balanced-/dense-/extreme- prefix; any other planner ID yields Unsupported UnsupportedRequiredFeature, so such encrypted archives cannot have recipients removed or passwords changed.
decision_needed: Should rotation fall back to preserving the existing plan instead of refusing?

statement: inspect_encrypted without unlock returns only public inspection after full public-framing validation (digests, structure, envelope policy); with unlock it performs a full authenticated open and ArchiveInspection.
evidence_in_source: test crypto_v1.rs L67-89; CLI test crypto_cli.rs hybrid_pack_public_inspect_verify_and_unpack

statement: Encrypted archives must be at least 448 bytes (256 preamble + 192 footer, else Truncated), carry Entrybound MAGIC (else BadMagic), format version 0.1 and preamble length 256 (else Unsupported UnsupportedVersion).

Encrypted readers require ENCRYPTED_INDEXED_V1, PAYLOAD_SUITE_V1 and PADDING bits, forbid STREAM_LAYOUT_V1, CONVERSION_PROVENANCE_V1 and LEGACY_PRESERVATION_V1, and refuse unknown bits with CryptoSuiteUnsupported before any recipient work.
Encrypted STREAM layout is not supported: readers refuse stream-layout-v1 with encryption, and the CLI refuses encrypted STREAM or stdout output with CryptoLayoutUnsupported before emitting bytes.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L752 and L764; docs/crypto-suite-v1.md L846-847 (CRYPTO-032); docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md L217-219; crates/entrybound-cli/src/lib.rs:690-696
decision_needed: Is an encrypted STREAM (unseekable/pipe) layout required post-v1?

statement: Encryption cannot be combined with conversion-provenance-v1 or legacy-preservation-v1 archives; such feature sets are refused as invalid encrypted feature sets.
decision_needed: Must legacy-preserving or provenance-carrying conversions be encryptable in v1?

statement: Encrypted preamble sentinels: bytes 24-40 (read-only-compat and compat feature words) zero, feature digest at 40-72 correct, byte 72 = 1 (INDEXED), byte 73 = 1 (Complete), byte 74 = 0, all bytes from 75 zero; violations are NoncanonicalEncoding.

Encrypted archives cannot use read-only-compatible or compatible feature bits, cannot publish a public resource budget in the preamble, and must have Complete role; partial/incremental encrypted archive roles are unsupported.
decision_needed: How will encrypted archives adopt optional (compat) features or partial roles without breaking v1 readers?

statement: Footer total length must equal EOF (Corrupt IncorrectTotalLength), footer preamble digest must match (FooterBindingMismatch), envelope must start at 256, segments must follow it contiguously and end exactly at the footer (SectionStructure).
Before KDF or KEM work the reader enforces CryptoEnvelope payload <= max_envelope_bytes (16 MiB default), stanza count <= max_stanzas (1024), and each encoded stanza <= max_stanza_bytes (65536).
An unkeyed SHA-256 over the complete EncryptedSegments payload, stored in the footer, must match; it detects accidental corruption without keys but an attacker can recompute it.
Keyless scan_public_segments walks all SegmentHeaders enforcing max_segments (1,000,000 default), max_messages_per_segment, extent <= max_working_memory_bytes (1 GiB default) and no truncation.

The SHA-256 of the PublicCryptoContext (versions, suite, archive ID, layout, role, features, padding, boundary) must match the footer and the envelope protection policy must agree with stanzas and feature bits before unlocking.

unlock_envelope tries stanzas in order, pairing identities only with type 1 and passwords only with type 2; wrap-AEAD failures continue silently; attempts are capped by max_identity_attempts; no success yields CryptoNoMatchingRecipient.
evidence_in_source: tests crypto_v1.rs L148-211, L479-511 (unknown stanza type and malformed encapsulation both yield CryptoNoMatchingRecipient)

statement: Unlock cost is linear in stanza count (up to 1024 X-Wing decapsulations); default max_identity_attempts 4096 exceeds max_stanzas 1024 so it never binds; early return on first match may expose matching-stanza position via timing.
research_needed: Measure worst-case unlock latency with 1024 stanzas; assess timing side channel revealing recipient position to local or remote observers.
decision_needed: Should max_identity_attempts default below max_stanzas or unlock be constant-work?

statement: After a wrap opens, key commitment is checked in constant time before the envelope MAC; a commitment or MAC failure is a hard Corrupt error (CryptoKeyCommitmentFailed/CryptoEnvelopeAuthFailed), not a continue to other stanzas.
research_needed: External review that hard-failing on commitment mismatch cannot be abused to deny unlock for other legitimate recipients (multi-recipient poisoning).

statement: Per-segment key: HKDF-SHA256 extract with the 16-byte segment salt over the CONTROL or PAYLOAD root, expanded with T1 segment-key/v1 over archive ID, suite, class and ordinal; CONTROL and PAYLOAD roots are distinct.
evidence_in_source: frozen vector in mod.rs test frozen_v1_to_v4_construction_vectors

statement: AES-256-GCM-SIV nonces: DATA = 00000000 || counter u64be; END = ffffffff || DATA count u64be; uniqueness relies on a unique key per segment salt/ordinal.
evidence_in_source: unit test padding_and_nonce_rules_are_frozen container.rs L2919-2935; V2 vectors

statement: Record associated data is T1 aead-record/v1 over FORMAT_NAMESPACE, crypto version, payload suite, archive ID, exact 64-byte SegmentHeader and exact ProtectedRecordHeader.

Every crypto transcript binds FORMAT_NAMESPACE ecf/bootstrap-v1 and format version 0.1, which ecf.rs describes as experimental with a candidate magic; renaming the namespace or version at format freeze would change all crypto vectors and invalidate existing encrypted archives.
decision_needed: Will the bootstrap namespace/version 0.1 be the permanent v1 identity bound into crypto transcripts?

statement: ProtectedRecordHeader: magic EBC1, version 1, record class, zero byte, ordinal and counter equal to position, ciphertext length >= 16 and <= max_ciphertext_record_bytes (64 MiB + 16); reordered or noncanonical records are CryptoSegmentStructureInvalid.
SegmentHeader: magic EBSG, version 1, class CONTROL or PAYLOAD, zero byte, ordinal equal to position, 16-byte salt, DATA count <= 2^20-1, reserved bytes 36-48 and 56-64 zero, extent >= 112 bytes.

Each segment holds exactly its declared DATA records then one END record and nothing after; END authenticates ordinal, class, DATA count, aggregate unpadded private bytes, aggregate ciphertext bytes and DATA transcript digest.

Full reader computes each completed segment digest (header, DATA, END header, END ciphertext) and requires ArchiveFinal's prior segment-sequence digest to equal the ordered nonterminal digests, preventing segment splicing, reordering, or omission.
evidence_in_source: tests splice_first_segment and reorder crypto_v1.rs L513-535

statement: Terminal segment must be CONTROL with one DATA record completing exactly one object (ArchiveFinal); footer terminal and ArchiveFinal locators and ArchiveFinal segment count must equal actual positions.
evidence_in_source: test footer locator mutation crypto_v1.rs L546-552

statement: Authenticated ArchiveFinal must match recomputed FooterCore digest (FooterBindingMismatch), recipient-set digest, and Descriptor and Manifest encrypted object IDs (CryptoEnvelopeAuthFailed).
Embedded-signature collection presence must exactly match FEATURE_SIGNATURE_ED25519_V1.

Full reader derives ordinary features by removing crypto bits with read-only-compat/compat zero, requires ArchiveFinal LAI/PCR/AUX equal to Descriptor roots, and unique Chunk count equal to decoded Chunk frames.

ObjectCollector preallocates Vec::with_capacity(total_len) from a decrypted PrivateFragment without checking max_working_memory_bytes or the 1 GiB object limit; anyone with a recipient public key can author such a record, risking allocation abort. The range reader checks this bound.
refines_or_supersedes: contradicts docs/crypto-threat-model-v1.md §Resource safety L157-163 and docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md L158-165; compare random.rs:1356-1360
evidence_in_source: inference from code; decode_private_fragment (wire.rs:512-532) does not bound total_len
research_needed: Adversarial test/fuzz: authenticated archive with huge fragment total_len against open_encrypted.
decision_needed: Add caller-policy bound before allocation in the full reader?

statement: Fragments must start at index 0 offset 0 and be contiguous with identical object ID, total length and count; reassembled length and encrypted-object ID (SHA-256 T1 encrypted-object/v1) must match, else Corrupt CryptoPrivateObjectInvalid.
The full reader's object collector persists across segment boundaries, so it accepts objects fragmented across segments and multiple objects per segment, consistent with the wire specification.

Private objects must follow strict rank order (Descriptor 1, plans 2, groups 3, directory 4, dictionaries 5, reconstruction data 6, regions 7, Chunks 8 repeatable, Manifest 9, Fidelity 10, signatures 11, Index 12, ArchiveFinal 13); Descriptor first; duplicates or disorder refused.

Descriptor record version 2 must coincide with the private-resource-declaration feature; its declared budget and decode requirements are enforced against caller policy at dispatch, before dependent private objects are accepted.
CHUNK private objects need only EBCH frame magic at dispatch; full frame semantics are validated later by the ordinary ECF plain-parts opener.

Full open records only Index presence: Index entries are never decoded or validated, and a malformed Index container fails the whole open, whereas the range reader validates entries and tolerates or rebuilds an invalid Index.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L563-566 (reader ignores/rebuilds missing or invalid Index)
research_needed: Differential conformance tests for malformed Index across open_encrypted and open_indexed_random_encrypted.
decision_needed: Should the full reader validate Index entries, and should a malformed Index be fatal?

statement: Unknown private singleton records and unknown EBCS collection kinds are refused; there is no forward-compatible optional private object mechanism in crypto v1.
decision_needed: How will future optional private metadata be added without a new required feature bit?

statement: HYBRID_ONLY archives must contain a recipient directory with exactly one entry per type-1 stanza (matching ID set, type 1, 32-byte fingerprint, label <= 1024 bytes, no duplicates); PASSWORD archives must not contain one.

Envelope policy: HYBRID_ONLY needs >=1 stanza, no type 2, all class 1, XWING bit set and PASSWORD bit clear; PASSWORD_ONLY needs one type-2 class-2 stanza with PASSWORD bit and not XWING; known types need exact method parameters and encapsulation lengths.

Unknown stanza types with class 1 are tolerated in HYBRID_ONLY envelopes, skipped at unlock, counted in recipient count and recipient-set digest, and excluded from the directory; semantics for future recipient types are otherwise undefined.
decision_needed: What is the extension contract for new recipient stanza types (e.g. post-draft X-Wing)?

statement: Objects are fragmented into pieces of class capacity minus 512 bytes (1 MiB or 64 MiB minus 512); empty objects or objects over 1 GiB are refused.

Padding: NONE exact length; MAXIMUM pads every record to class maximum (1 MiB CONTROL, 64 MiB PAYLOAD); BUCKETED uses quarter-octave sizes {1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75} x 2^k, CONTROL 256 B-1 MiB, PAYLOAD 4 KiB-64 MiB, including the 8-byte length prefix.
evidence_in_source: unit test padding_and_nonce_rules_are_frozen container.rs L2919-2935; round trip test every_padding_mode_round_trips crypto_v1.rs L370-393

statement: Bucketed padding overhead (suite doc models 6.7-11.1% mean, <25% worst) is unmeasured; every PAYLOAD record pays at least 4 KiB, so small-file or small-Chunk archives may inflate substantially.
research_needed: Measure padded size overhead and privacy gain on real corpora (source trees, photo sets, many small files).

statement: With one object per segment, MAXIMUM padding makes every PAYLOAD segment about 65 MiB (64 MiB record plus 1 MiB END) regardless of Chunk size, so archive size is roughly 65 MiB per unique Chunk.
research_needed: Measure MAXIMUM-padded archive size and creation/open time on small corpora.
decision_needed: Should MAXIMUM padding remain a user-selectable v1 mode, and with what warnings or limits?

statement: END records are padded with CONTROL bucket and capacity rules even inside PAYLOAD segments.

Padding bytes are fresh OS CSPRNG output inside the AEAD; after decryption the 8-byte private length must fit and total plaintext must equal the padded length for class and mode, else CryptoPaddingInvalid.
build_segment seals all fragments before enforcing the 1 GiB per-segment unpadded limit, so an oversize segment is detected only after encryption work.

Writer preamble: MAGIC, version 0.1, length 256, incompat features, zero compat words, feature digest, layout 1, role 1, all else zero. Section header: EBS1, kind, version 1, reserved zeros, payload length, payload SHA-256, reserved zeros.

FooterCoreV1 transcript T1 encrypted-footer-core/v1 covers footer version 2, total length, envelope and segments offsets/lengths, terminal and ArchiveFinal offsets, preamble digest and public-context digest, but not the unkeyed segments digest.

Recipient-set digest is SHA-256 of T1 recipient-set/v1 over the canonical stanza sequence; RecipientDirectoryEntryV1 (record 22) tags are stanza ID, type (=1), fingerprint, UTF-8 label; only type-1 entries can be re-encoded during mutation.
Encrypted Descriptor roots are read from record type 1: version 1 must have exactly tags 1-8, version 2 exactly tags 1-19; LAI, PCR, AUX are tags 6, 7, 8.

Secret-dependent comparisons (commitment, MAC, footer-core, recipient-set, segment-sequence, identity roots, SegmentEnd digest) use subtle constant-time equality; public digest comparisons use ordinary equality.
research_needed: Side-channel review of the AES-GCM-SIV, Argon2 and X-Wing dependencies and remaining variable-time paths.

statement: Container diagnostics: structural segment faults are Nonconforming CryptoSegmentStructureInvalid; truncation is Truncated TruncatedStream; binding/tag failures are Corrupt; policy limits are PolicyRefused CryptoResourcePolicyRefused.

AFK-preserving mutations produce sibling archives sharing archive ID and segment keys; the full reader's segment-sequence digest blocks cross-version splicing, but no freshness or rollback protection exists between versions.
research_needed: Formal/symbolic analysis of splicing across AFK-sharing sibling archives for both full and range readers.

statement: In-file tests: padding_and_nonce_rules_are_frozen, corrected_writer_emits_v2_feature_and_legacy_v1_remains_readable, descriptor_feature_mismatch_duplicate_and_missing_fail_closed, authenticated_underdeclared_budget_and_decode_are_rejected, recipient_addition_reuses_bulk_payload_ciphertext.

Integration tests covering container.rs: hybrid round trip privacy, private manifest metadata, private-resource feature forbidden unencrypted, multiple recipients, password unlock, signature/recipient mutation staleness, password rotation, keyed CDC pack, all padding modes, tamper/truncation, reordering/splicing/policy, unknown feature.
research_needed: Add fuzzing and hostile-sender adversarial corpora (oversized fragments, reordered CONTROL objects, multi-object segments).

statement: open_indexed_random_encrypted opens a crypto-v1 INDEXED archive over any RandomReadSource (memory, local file, HTTP range) and authenticates CONTROL records without reading unrelated PAYLOAD segments.

inspect_indexed_random_encrypted_public performs keyless range inspection: footer, preamble, envelope and every SegmentHeader; reports public crypto fields, source revision, required features, bytes fetched, range request count, access trace, and whole_archive_verified false.

Range readers validate the preamble with generic decode_preamble, which allows nonzero compat words, byte 74 of 1 and public budget bytes, and neither require PADDING nor forbid provenance/legacy bits; the full reader rejects these, so the two readers accept different byte sets.
refines_or_supersedes: contradicts docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L131-140 (zero public budget sentinels under 0x20); compare crates/entrybound/src/crypto/container.rs:1065-1093 and crates/entrybound/src/ecf/container.rs:2692-2800
research_needed: Differential conformance corpus of preamble variants across open_encrypted and range opener.
decision_needed: Should the encrypted range reader apply the same canonical preamble checks as the full reader?

statement: Public range inspection checks envelope length and stanza count but not per-stanza byte size; the unlocking range opener checks all three limits.
Encrypted range access requires RandomAccessPolicy.max_section_count >= 2 (RandomAccessPolicyRefused) and a source length of at least 448 bytes (Truncated).

The range opener unlocks with the shared unlock_envelope (commitment and MAC checks), drops the AFK immediately, but keeps the derived KeyHierarchy (including segment roots) for the lifetime of the session, zeroized on drop.
research_needed: Review in-memory key exposure duration for long-lived range sessions.

statement: At open, every CONTROL segment is fetched and decrypted, including recipient directory and signatures, with aggregate CONTROL private bytes bounded by max_working_memory_bytes.

The range opener enforces Descriptor-first and Descriptor-v2 declared budget/decode vs caller policy only when segment ordinal 0 is CONTROL, and checks no CONTROL object order; a hostile sender placing a PAYLOAD segment first bypasses those checks, unlike the full reader.
evidence_in_source: inference from code (check nested under ordinal == 0 after skipping non-CONTROL segments)
research_needed: Adversarial test: authenticated archive with PAYLOAD at ordinal 0 and inflated Descriptor-v2 budget opened via range reader.
decision_needed: Require CONTROL Descriptor at ordinal 0 and enforce full rank order in the range reader?

statement: Chunk bounds in range access use the producer's authenticated declared budget when present instead of caller resource policy; safety therefore depends on the declared-vs-caller check that can be skipped.
decision_needed: Should range chunk bounds use the minimum of declared budget and caller policy?

statement: Range opener requires authenticated ArchiveFinal and terminal bindings, decodes Manifest and Fidelity, verifies LAI and AUX from metadata, checks entry count and Descriptor roots against ArchiveFinal, and checks Manifest content references.

Range reader ignores ArchiveFinal's prior segment-sequence digest and the footer's segments digest; CONTROL objects besides Descriptor/Manifest (TransformPlans, ChunkGroups, Index) are not bound to the terminal, so sibling-version CONTROL segments sharing keys might be spliced undetected.
refines_or_supersedes: contradicts docs/crypto-implementation-v1.md L143-146 (ArchiveFinal validates ordered completed-segment digest)
research_needed: Formal splice/substitution analysis for range reads, especially after AFK-preserving embed_signature/add_recipient; design a per-segment digest table for partial verification.
decision_needed: Should ArchiveFinal or a CONTROL object bind per-segment digests usable by partial readers?

statement: Range opener's ordinary FeatureSet copies preamble read-only-compat and compat words, whereas the full reader forces them to zero.
TransformPlans decode as v3 when whole-object reconstruction is required, v2 when reconstructive, else v1 with codec-transform flag, then validate; ChunkGroups decoded when present.

Synthesized encrypted descriptor hard-codes INDEXED layout, Complete role, stream_dedup_window 0, IdentityV1, SHA-256, and no PCI; pre-correction archives get budget_declared false with default ResourceBudget and DecodeRequirements.

Encrypted Index status is PresentValid when entries decode and count matches ArchiveFinal, RebuiltInvalid when the container or entries are malformed, and RebuiltAbsent when missing; an invalid Index is never fatal in range access.
RandomAccessMetadata for encrypted archives lists two sections (CryptoEnvelope, EncryptedSegments), the encrypted segment count, and encrypted=true.

read_entry decodes the requested file's Chunk closure (lookback predecessors, whole-object reconstruction regions), verifies each Chunk digest, chunk root, content digest and sparse map, bounded by max_dependency_chunks and max_decoded_logical_bytes.
No byte-range read inside an entry: the whole entry plaintext is reconstructed and returned in memory, limited only by max_decoded_logical_bytes (8 GiB default).
research_needed: Measure latency and memory for reading large single files (e.g. VM images) from remote encrypted archives.
decision_needed: Is sub-entry byte-range read required for v1 remote/encrypted access?

statement: Range read of directories, symlinks and reparse points is refused with Unsupported RandomAccessEntryNotFile; only files with internal content references are readable.

On first read, all PAYLOAD segments not referenced by a valid Index are fetched and decrypted (Dictionaries, ReconstructionData, Regions, and all Chunks when Index is absent/invalid), bounded by max_working_memory_bytes and max_chunk_frames_scanned; aggregate decode requirements must equal declared and satisfy caller decode policy.

Without a valid encrypted Index the first read degrades to fetching and retaining every PAYLOAD segment, capped by 1 GiB retained private bytes, so larger archives created with include_index=false are effectively not range-readable.
evidence_in_source: inference from code; test only covers tiny archive
research_needed: Measure bytes fetched and failure threshold for Index-less encrypted archives over HTTP.
decision_needed: Should the encrypted Index be mandatory for archives intended for remote access?

statement: If a valid Index exists but an unindexed PAYLOAD segment holds a Chunk, status flips to RebuiltInvalid and the Index map is replaced by only Chunks from unindexed segments, discarding indexed Chunks and causing count mismatch or missing-Chunk errors.
research_needed: Construct an authenticated archive with an extra unindexed Chunk segment and observe range read behavior.

statement: chunk_frame caches decrypted frames and, on any Index inconsistency (wrong class, fragment count, object kind or digest), clears support and falls back to a full PAYLOAD rescan.

The decrypted chunk_frames cache has no byte bound across repeated read_entry calls (only the fallback scan and session range cache are bounded), so long sessions can accumulate most decrypted frames in memory.
research_needed: Memory profiling of many sequential read_entry calls on one encrypted session.

statement: For prefix/lookback plans, predecessors are up to lookback preceding Chunks in segment-ordinal order sharing the group; group lookback must equal the plan's and preceding logical bytes must not exceed group max_preceding_bytes (Corrupt AccessCostMismatch).

decode_chunk recursively decodes predecessors, refuses independent decode of region-owned Chunks, verifies plaintext digest equals Chunk ID, and bounds retained decoded bytes by max_decoded_logical_bytes.

Encrypted range reports hard-code source revision stable, preamble/footer, section structure and semantic metadata verified; LAI and AUX Verified, PCR DeclaredNotFullyVerified, PCI NotComputed, whole_archive_verified false.

dictionaries_verified and groups_verified are set to cross-file feature presence rather than whether the requested entry actually used and verified a Dictionary or ChunkGroup, so reports may overclaim verification.
decision_needed: Should report flags reflect objects actually exercised by the read?

statement: No range-based whole-archive verification exists for encrypted archives: PCI is never computed and PCR never fully verified; whole-archive verification needs full download and open_encrypted.
decision_needed: Is remote incremental whole-archive verification of encrypted archives required?

statement: Range envelope read: extent between 64 bytes and max_metadata_bytes (128 MiB default), canonical section kind 32 header, header payload length consistent with footer extent, and payload SHA-256 match.

walk_segments issues one 64-byte range read per SegmentHeader, enforcing max_segments, max_encrypted_segment_header_walk, count and extent limits, per-class salt uniqueness, containment, and a terminal CONTROL single-record segment at footer locators.

Because writers use one segment per object (about one per unique Chunk), encrypted open needs one range request per segment; default max_range_requests 100,000 would refuse archives with roughly 100k+ Chunks despite the 4,000,000 header-walk limit, and HTTP latency scales with Chunk count.
research_needed: Measure open-time request count and latency vs unique Chunk count over real HTTP/S3 endpoints.
decision_needed: Add a CONTROL segment-locator table or coalesced header prefetch for encrypted range open?

statement: decrypt_segment fetches a whole segment in one range; MAXIMUM-padded PAYLOAD segments (~65 MiB) and any single CONTROL object above ~64 MiB (e.g. large Manifest) exceed default max_individual_range_bytes 64 MiB, so default range access likely refuses them.
research_needed: Test default-policy range open of MAXIMUM-padded archives and archives with >64 MiB Manifests.

statement: The range reader requires every segment to contain exactly one complete object starting at fragment 0 and Index first_counter 0, but the wire spec allows objects spanning segments and the full reader accepts them; spec-conforming archives from other writers may be range-unreadable.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L533-534 and L554-562 (first protected-record counter field)
decision_needed: Narrow the wire spec to one-object-per-segment or generalize the range reader?

statement: Range reader refuses a declared object total length above max_working_memory_bytes before reserving memory.
A fetched segment's header must equal the header observed during the walk, and the source revision must remain stable at open and after each read.

Range CONTROL dispatch accepts Descriptor, Fidelity, ArchiveFinal, TransformPlans, ChunkGroups, Manifest and Index, silently ignores RecipientDirectory and Signatures, refuses PAYLOAD collections or Chunks in CONTROL, and treats a malformed Index container as index_invalid.

Range access neither decodes nor validates embedded signatures or the recipient directory and does not check signature feature/collection agreement, so no signature or directory information is available through the range opener.
decision_needed: Should remote/range opening expose and verify embedded signatures?

statement: The pre-correction form without the private-resource-declaration feature is explicitly accepted by range access as a supported legacy encrypted Descriptor v1.

Encrypted Index validation: record 27 with tags 1-4, 32-byte digest, existing PAYLOAD segment, first counter 0, nonzero fragment count equal to the segment's record count, no duplicate digests, total equal to ArchiveFinal unique Chunk count.

Range footer parsing classifies declared total length above source length as Truncated and below as Corrupt, and labels noncanonical footers CryptoPrivateObjectInvalid, unlike the full reader's NoncanonicalEncoding; diagnostics differ by reader.
decision_needed: Unify reason codes across encrypted readers?

statement: random.rs re-implements segment header, protected header, record decryption, padding schedule, DATA transcript and SegmentEnd validation instead of sharing container.rs code, creating drift risk between readers.
research_needed: Differential testing/fuzzing of both encrypted readers on shared corpora.
decision_needed: Consolidate shared crypto framing parsers into one module?

statement: Range opener rejects Manifest file Entries that reference unknown ContentObjects with Corrupt RandomAccessDependencyInvalid.

Corruption in an unread PAYLOAD segment does not prevent reading another entry, and reports never claim whole-archive verification (PCI NotComputed), localizing blast radius for encrypted range reads.
Password-protected archives are range-readable; Argon2id and decryption run client-side under the same policy-checked unlock path.

Remote encrypted reads fetch less than the whole archive, but tests only assert bytes_fetched below source length on tiny fixtures; no measured fetched fraction, request count, or latency at realistic scale.
research_needed: Benchmark encrypted range reads on large archives against HTTP/S3 with realistic RTT, reporting bytes, requests and latency.

statement: Only two recipient methods exist: X-Wing draft-10 hybrid public keys and one Argon2id password; classical-only (e.g. X25519-only) recipients are not implemented.
decision_needed: Are classical-only recipients needed for interoperability (e.g. age/SSH keys) post-v1?

statement: Unlock accepts only an in-memory X-Wing identity or password bytes; no KMS, HSM, hardware token, agent or plugin unlock path exists.
decision_needed: Is external key-custody unlock (KMS/HSM/agent) required for v1 adoption?

statement: Recipient removal produces a new re-encrypted archive but cannot revoke plaintext or old archive copies already held by removed recipients.
evidence_in_source: design statement in suite doc; code only emits replacement bytes

statement: The writer still accepts Descriptor-v1 plain parts (emitting the legacy form without 0x1000), reachable in-crate only through the cfg(test) prepare_legacy_encrypted_plain_parts helper; the spec says writers never emit this form.
refines_or_supersedes: docs/crypto-wire-v1.md L147-152 (writers never emit legacy form); crates/entrybound/src/ecf.rs:85-86
decision_needed: Should encrypt_with_material hard-refuse Descriptor v1 outside tests?
